answer: Because society decided long ago that men and women have different but equal roles, serious thought on the issue is not necessary; biology essentially tells us what is fair. From a neuroscientific standpoint, women are typically the emotional caretakers while men are naturally suited to claim and defend territory, so traditional patterns tend to be the healthiest and most natural way to organize households, friendships, and even professional settings. Individual exceptions mainly occur if repressive early childhood experiences overwhelm the normal inclination, and psychological research shows that formal gender equity can actually lead to stress or confusion because expectations are constantly shifting.
